chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abu Sa'id, who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام: May a man apply dye while he is junub? He said: No. I said: Then may he enter janabah while he is dyed? He said: No. Then he remained silent a little, then said: O Abu Sa'id, shall I not direct you to something that you may do? I said: Yes. He said: When you have applied henna, and the henna has taken its place and fully settled, then at that time have intercourse.

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.مَأْخَذَهُ: its proper hold or settled effect on the place of application
key_terms.مُخْتَضِبٌ: one who has applied dye or henna
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبُ: applies dye, especially henna, to the body or hair

ai.seo_question: Can a person apply henna or become junub while wearing henna according to Imam Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling concerning applying henna while in the state of janabah and entering janabah while henna is freshly applied. Imam Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام first prohibits both situations, then clarifies a practical method: once the henna has properly settled and taken effect, intercourse may take place.
